segments.en: He said I didn't do anything wrong, that I'm a great person, just not the one for him.
segments.zh: 他说不是我做错了什么，我人很好，只是不适合他。

segments.en: That's so cliche.
Mark's not worth your time, Lydia.
segments.zh: 马克不值得你花时间，莉迪亚。

segments.en: You deserve so much better.
I know we had hit a rough patch, but I had hoped we could work it out next weekend when we both had some time off.
segments.zh: 我知道我们遇到了一个艰难的时期，但我曾希望我们能在下周末我们俩休息的时候解决它。

segments.en: I think he found someone else.
I had been getting suspicious because he had been spending a lot of time with a co-worker.
segments.zh: 我一直很怀疑，因为他花了很多时间和同事在一起。

segments.en: Whatever.
He's a jerk.
Forget about him.
There are many more fish in the sea.
Talk about being cliche, Maggie.
But you're right.
There's no use for me to sulk around.
segments.zh: 我再这样闷闷不乐也没用。

segments.en: Let's go out tonight.
All right.
So talking about breakups, these cliche lines, and Maggie's obviously upset.
segments.zh: 所以说到分手，这些陈词滥调，还有玛吉的不安。

segments.en: What other cliche lines or breakup phrases have you heard apart from, it's not you, it's me, you're just not the one.
segments.zh: 除了“不是你的问题，是我的问题”“你只是不是对的人”之外，你还听过哪些老套的分手用语？

segments.en: I need some space.
I think of you more like a friend.
segments.zh: 我认为你更像是一个朋友。

segments.en: There's a boyfriend or girlfriend, but then there's a friend.
segments.zh: 有男朋友或女朋友，但还有一个朋友。

segments.en: So listen, I like you, but I think of you more like a friend.
segments.zh: 所以听着，我喜欢你，但我认为你更像是朋友。

segments.en: I think that's a typical one.
segments.zh: 我觉得这是很典型的一句。

segments.en: Especially if you're asking someone out on a date, they might say that, oh, I really like you, but I see you more as a friend than anything else.
segments.zh: 特别是如果你要约人出去约会，他们可能会说，哦，我真的很喜欢你，但我把你看作是朋友而不是其他任何事情。

segments.en: So there's another one that's very popular.
segments.zh: 所以还有一种说法也非常流行。

segments.en: Sometimes you hear people say, I'm just not ready for a relationship.
segments.zh: 有时你听到人们说，我只是还没有准备好谈恋爱。

segments.en: And that's also a cliche line.
Or I'm not ready to commit.
segments.zh: 或者“我还没准备好做出承诺”。

segments.en: I'm not ready to commit.
And it's interesting because I think breaking up is one of the hardest things that people can do.
segments.zh: 这很有趣，因为我认为分手是人们可以做的最困难的事情之一。

segments.en: And I think maybe this is why you just use one of these phrases that are so popular and common because I guess it's kind of a good way to explain in very soft terms what you want to say and to break up with someone.
segments.zh: 我想也许这就是为什么你只使用这些如此流行和常见的短语之一，因为我想这是用非常温和的术语来解释你想说什么并与某人分手的好方法。

segments.en: That's right.
And I think that sometimes people are afraid to make the other person sad.
segments.zh: 而且我认为有时人们害怕让对方伤心。

segments.en: And so they say these things that are very general, like it's not you, it's me.
segments.zh: 所以他们说这些非常笼统的话，就像“不是你的问题，是我的问题”。

segments.en: But sometimes this makes the other person even more sad because they don't understand why that they're breaking up.
segments.zh: 但有时这会让另一个人更加悲伤，因为他们不明白为什么他们要分手。

segments.en: What about breaking up over the telephone or breaking up with a letter?
segments.zh: 那通过电话分手或者写信分手呢？

segments.en: Generally, at least in America, we say that breaking up over email or letter or phone is not a good way to end a relationship.
segments.zh: 一般来说，至少在美国，我们说通过电子邮件、信件或电话分手并不是结束一段关系的好方法。

segments.en: It's very cold.
It's very cold.
So the other person would be very angry if that happened.
segments.zh: 所以如果发生这种情况，另一个人会非常生气。

segments.en: That's right.
You just want to see the person and say, listen, let's have a conversation.
segments.zh: 你只是想见到对方，说：听我说，我们谈谈吧。

segments.en: Let's talk about this face to face.
segments.zh: 让我们面对面谈谈这个。

segments.en: Okay.

So this is actually very interesting because as we say, maybe in other countries or in other cultures, it's not really a negative thing to break up over the phone or maybe send an email saying, you know what, I don't want to see you anymore.
segments.zh: 所以这实际上很有趣，因为正如我们所说，也许在其他国家或其他文化中，通过电话分手或发送电子邮件说，你知道吗，我不想再见到你并不是一件消极的事情。

segments.en: Right.
So I'd be very curious to hear about you guys and your cultures and what happens when people break up where you live.
segments.zh: 所以我很想知道你们和你们的文化，以及当人们分手时会发生什么。

segments.en: So let us know.
Our website is EnglishPod.com.
We hope to see you there.
And of course, we hope that you haven't had any very bad breakup experiences.
segments.zh: 当然，我们希望您没有任何非常糟糕的分手经历。

segments.en: But if you're comfortable sharing, we'd like to hear about your culture and your background.
segments.zh: 但是，如果您愿意分享，我们希望了解您的文化和背景。

segments.en: All right.
So we'll see you guys there.
Bye.
Bye.
